title: Staged residency and KV-shadowing to reduce cold-start tail latency
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets still experience long cold-start tail latency when tenants spike or when model residency churns (weight load time and KV cache miss overhead). Existing warm-pool heuristics are reactive and can over-hold weights, increasing cost, or under-hold and cause high p95/p99 cold starts.

Proposal: Implement a two-part system: (1) staged-residency controller that creates short-lived micro-residency windows based on predicted request arrivals and tenant SLAs; (2) KV-shadowing — a background, low-priority request fanout that mirrors a subset of incoming traffic to populate KV caches and warm relevant activation paths without affecting production latency or billing.

Key components:
- Residency allocator: holds model weights in GPU memory in staged time-windows (e.g., 15s, 60s, 5m) with smoothing to prevent thrash across tenants. Uses request-derived score + commitment hints from Dedicated reservations to set residency time.
- Shadowing worker: issues low-QoS inference calls against a pinned model variant to populate KV caches and prefetch attention/kv shards. Shadow requests are metered separately and can be disabled per-tenant.
- Admission controller integration: prioritizes live requests over shadow traffic and coordinates with autoscaler to avoid false scale-ups. Introduces backpressure to shadow queue under high CPU/GPU utilization.
- Cost controls: per-tenant shadow budget, global shadow budget, and heuristics to only shadow requests that have high cache priming value (e.g., long prefix, large context switches, or cold code-paths).

Design trade-offs:
- Cost vs latency: shadowing increases token/compute spend; we mitigate via selective sampling and per-tenant budgets.
- Accuracy of predictions: residency windows rely on short-term forecasting; mispredictions increase churn. We'll use conservative default windows and adapt via feedback loop.
- Interaction with autoscaling: avoid shadow-driven scale-outs. Shadow requests are weighted zero for scale and routed to spare capacity or low-priority partitions.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- p95 cold-start latency for typical Dedicated models reduced by >=50% in canary fleet vs baseline.
- End-to-end cost delta from shadowing < +5% for tenants that opt in (goal < +2% for default profile).
- No increase in live-request error rate or tail latency during shadowing.

Rollout plan: spec -> internal canary on 1 dedicated cluster -> expand to 5 clusters with controlled tenants -> enable opt-in for customers -> GA. Monitoring and kill-switch in Console.

Interactions: depends on autoscaler heuristics (ENG-110234) and Dedicated routing policies. Will add Console controls and per-tenant toggles in a follow-up.

References: design doc, cost model spreadsheet, and initial bench results attached below.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design (RFC) posted and reviewed by runtime and infra leads. Key feedback: ensure shadow requests never affect autoscaling signals.
2026-03-05: Prototype residency controller implemented (allocator + smoothing) and tested on a 4-node canary cluster. Basic timers and eviction logic wired.
2026-03-06: Shadowing worker MVP submitted (local loop) and integrated with admission controller. Shadow requests run at 1% sampling of incoming traffic for canary tenants.

2026-03-08: Benchmarks on model-replica-xx (13B) show baseline p95 cold-start = 12.6s, staged-residency alone reduced p95 to 6.2s; with KV-shadowing p95 reduced to 3.4s. Observed shadow cost +2.3% on canary tenants.
2026-03-09: Security review stubbed out; no sensitive data is written by shadow requests. Confirmed shadow requests do not emit customer billing events in canary mode.
2026-03-10: Open PRs for allocator and shadow worker; need infra review for admission-controller changes and a perf signoff for scaled shadow traffic.
Blocker: Pending autoscaler change to ignore shadow traffic for scale metrics (tracking ENG-110234).
acceptance_criteria: Canary cluster p95 cold-start reduced by >=50% vs baseline for 13B/70B tiers
Shadowing cost impact for opt-in tenants < +5% (goal < +2%)
No increase in production error rate or tail latency observed during canary
Autoscaler (ENG-110234) excludes shadow traffic for scale decisions
Console exposes per-tenant shadow toggle and global kill-switch
notes: Next steps: finalize autoscaler exemption, add per-tenant budgeting in Console, and run a 2-week extended canary with real traffic patterns.
If shadow cost is higher than expected, fall back to model-variant caching (lower precision, smaller memory) as a mitigation.
Long-term: consider predictive residency informed by historical diurnal patterns and customer SLA tiers.
